questions.stem: Which river is known as the 'Ganga of the South' due to its religious and cultural significance in peninsular India?
questions.explanation: The Godavari is called the 'Ganga of the South' (Dakshina Ganga). It is the longest peninsular river (~1465 km), originating near Nasik in Maharashtra and flowing east into the Bay of Bengal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Hirakud Dam, the longest dam in India (approximately 26 km), is built on which river in Odisha?
questions.explanation: The Hirakud Dam is constructed on the Mahanadi River near Sambalpur in Odisha. Built in 1957, it was one of the first major multipurpose river valley projects in post-independence India and remains the longest earthen dam in the world.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The river Brahmaputra, known as Tsangpo in Tibet, is called by what name in Bangladesh?
questions.explanation: The Brahmaputra is called the Tsangpo in Tibet, Brahmaputra in India (Assam), and Jamuna in Bangladesh. It eventually merges with the Ganga (called Padma in Bangladesh) and Meghna before emptying into the Bay of Bengal.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Bhakra Nangal Dam, the highest gravity dam in Asia, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on the Sutlej River on the Punjab-Himachal Pradesh border. Completed in 1963, it is one of the largest multi-purpose river valley projects in India and provides irrigation and power to Punjab, Haryana, and Rajasthan.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Godavari River, the longest peninsular river of India, originates near which city in Maharashtra?
questions.explanation: The Godavari originates from the Brahmagiri hills near Trimbakeshwar, close to Nasik (Nashik) in Maharashtra at an altitude of about 1,067 m. It flows ~1,465 km and drains into the Bay of Bengal after passing through Telangana and Andhra Pradesh.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which Himalayan river is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' due to its frequent and devastating floods?
questions.explanation: The Kosi River is called the 'Sorrow of Bihar' because it frequently changes its course and causes devastating floods in the plains of Bihar. The river has shifted its course westward by about 120 km over the past 250 years.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Narmada River originates from which place in Madhya Pradesh?
questions.explanation: The Narmada originates at Amarkantak in the Maikal Range (part of the Satpura-Vindhya junction) in Madhya Pradesh at an altitude of 1,057 m. Remarkably, the Son River also originates at Amarkantak but flows eastward, while the Narmada flows westward into the Arabian Sea.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Chambal River, originating in Madhya Pradesh, is a major tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Chambal River originates in the Vindhya Range near Mhow (MP) and flows through MP, Rajasthan, and UP before joining the Yamuna River in Uttar Pradesh. The Chambal Valley is known for its ravines (badlands) and is a biodiversity hotspot.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam, one of the world's largest masonry dams, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is constructed on the Krishna River at the Telangana-Andhra Pradesh border. Completed in 1967, it is used for irrigation and hydroelectric power and is named after the ancient Buddhist philosopher Nagarjuna.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The river Damodar, a tributary of the Hooghly/Ganga system, is called the 'Sorrow of Bengal' because:
options: Its recurrent floods have historically devastated Bengal's farmlands
It is used for irrigation in Bengal only
British exploited its resources for coal transport
questions.explanation: The Damodar River, flowing through Jharkhand and West Bengal, caused frequent and catastrophic floods in the Bengal plains. The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC, set up 1948 — modelled on the Tennessee Valley Authority) was established to control its floods and harness its hydroelectric potential.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which peninsular river originates at Mahabaleshwar in Maharashtra and flows eastward into the Bay of Bengal?
questions.explanation: The Krishna River originates near Mahabaleshwar in the Western Ghats (Maharashtra) and flows eastward through Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh before emptying into the Bay of Bengal near Hamasaladeevi. It is India's third-longest river at ~1,400 km.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Kaveri River, a major source of water conflict between Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, originates in which state?
questions.explanation: The Kaveri (Cauvery) originates at Talakaveri in Kodagu (Coorg) district, Karnataka, in the Western Ghats at an altitude of 1,341 m. It flows southeast through Karnataka and Tamil Nadu before entering the Bay of Bengal at Poompuhar.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Sivasamudram Falls on the Kaveri River is historically significant because:
options: It was the site of Asia's first hydroelectric power station (1902)
It provides drinking water to Bengaluru city
It is at the site of Brindavan Gardens
questions.explanation: The Sivasamudram (Shivanasamudra) Falls in Karnataka was the site of Asia's first hydroelectric power station, commissioned in 1902. The power generated here was transmitted to Kolar Gold Fields — one of the earliest long-distance power transmissions in the world.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which of the following Himalayan rivers does NOT originate outside India (i.e., it originates within Indian territory)?
questions.explanation: The Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier in Uttarakhand, India. In contrast, the Indus, Brahmaputra, and Sutlej all originate in Tibet (China) and enter India through the Himalayas, making them trans-boundary rivers.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Sardar Sarovar Project (SSP), a major multi-purpose dam project, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is constructed on the Narmada River in Gujarat, near Navagam village. It is one of the largest concrete dams in the world and was at the centre of a major displacement and environmental controversy (Narmada Bachao Andolan).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Dhuandhar Falls (meaning 'smoky cascade'), where the Narmada drops through the Marble Rocks near Jabalpur, is located on which river?
questions.explanation: The Dhuandhar Falls are on the Narmada River near Bhedaghat, Jabalpur (MP). The river squeezes through the white marble gorge, creating fine spray that looks like smoke (dhuan). The area is a popular tourist destination.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Tehri Dam, one of the world's highest dams, is constructed on which river in Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: The Tehri Dam is built on the Bhagirathi River (a headstream of the Ganga) in Tehri Garhwal, Uttarakhand. At 260.5 m, it is the tallest dam in India and one of the tallest in the world. The dam submerged the old Tehri town.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Tungabhadra River, an important irrigation and hydroelectric resource for Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh, is a tributary of which river?
questions.explanation: The Tungabhadra is formed by the confluence of the Tunga and Bhadra rivers at Koodli, Karnataka. It flows northeast and joins the Krishna River in Andhra Pradesh. The Tungabhadra Dam (Hospet, Karnataka) is a major irrigation project.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Indus River originates near which lake in Tibet?
questions.explanation: The Indus (Sindhu) River originates near Lake Mansarovar (Mapam Yumco) in Tibet at an altitude of about 5,500 m, near Mount Kailash. It flows northwest through Ladakh and Pakistan before emptying into the Arabian Sea.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Ken River, to be linked with the Betwa River in India's first major inter-linking river project, is a tributary of which major river?
questions.explanation: The Ken River originates in Satna district, MP, flows northeast, and joins the Yamuna River in Banda district, UP (near Banda town). The Ken-Betwa Link Project involves diverting surplus waters of the Ken to the Betwa basin in the Bundelkhand region.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Which river has been accorded the status of 'National River of India'?
questions.explanation: The Ganga was accorded the status of India's National River in 2008 by the National Ganga River Basin Authority. The Namami Gange programme was launched in 2014 to clean and rejuvenate the Ganga.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Mettur Dam, which controls the irrigation of the Kaveri Delta in Tamil Nadu, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Mettur Dam (Stanley Reservoir) is built on the Kaveri River in Salem district, Tamil Nadu. Completed in 1934, it is one of the largest dams in India and a major source of irrigation water for the Kaveri Delta.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Ganga River is formed at Devprayag in Uttarakhand by the confluence of which two rivers?
questions.explanation: The Ganga is formed at Devprayag (one of the Panch Prayag) by the confluence of the Bhagirathi (which originates at Gomukh, Gangotri Glacier) and the Alaknanda (which originates at Satopanth Glacier near Badrinath).
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Son River, a right-bank tributary of the Ganga flowing from south to north, also originates at which place in Madhya Pradesh — the same source area as the Narmada?
questions.explanation: Both the Narmada and the Son originate at Amarkantak (Maikal Hills), MP. The Narmada flows west into the Arabian Sea, while the Son flows northeast and joins the Ganga near Patna, Bihar. The contrast in flow direction from the same source is a classic geography exam point.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Ganga River is considered to originate at which glacier in Uttarakhand?
questions.explanation: The Bhagirathi — main headstream of the Ganga — emerges from the Gomukh (cow's mouth) at the snout of the Gangotri Glacier in Uttarkashi district, Uttarakhand, at an altitude of ~3,892 m. The Yamuna originates at Yamunotri Glacier.
questions.subject: Geography
